subject: BYOK & egress contract clarification for EdgeHealth private deployment
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@edgehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy questions — BYOK, subprocessors, and egress

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile for the Dedicated private deploy. Before we hand this to Legal/Procurement, a few security items they asked me to clarify around our VPC/on‑prem option:

- BYOK: we intend to manage our own keys (KMS in our cloud). Does Redwood support a bring‑your‑own‑key model for the private control plane? If so, what access (if any) do Redwood operators have to customer keys or plaintext?
- Subprocessors: can you provide the list of subprocessors that will touch telemetry/audit logs or runbook automation? We need a signed subprocessor appendix or confirmation that none of your subprocessors will have access to PII in the tenant.
- Egress/data flow: we need explicit contract language that disallows any model or inference data egress to third regions or to any third‑party analytics systems; EdgeHealth must retain control of all model inputs/outputs.
- Operator breakglass: for on‑prem installs, under what circumstances would Redwood ask for emergency access and how is that limited/recorded?

I attached a one‑page network sketch to show our intended VPC peering and NAT egress points. If you can send a short annex we can share with Legal, that would speed things up.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of InfoSec, EdgeHealth

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — BYOK, subprocessors, and egress

Alicia — thanks for the clear list and the diagram (attached). Below are concrete answers and an initial annex to propose to Legal. I'm copying Ben from Product so we have implementation/ops alignment.

1) BYOK model: yes, we support customer‑managed keys for Private (VPC and on‑prem). Typical modes:
   • Customer KMS (preferred): Redwood never holds the KEK; customer provides a key resource/endpoint and we use it to encrypt our local keystore. Redwood operators do not have direct access to customer KMS keys or plaintext under this configuration.
   • Escrow option: only used with explicit, contractually limited escrow (we provide procedures and audit trail). You indicated you prefer no escrow, which is fine.

2) Subprocessors: attached is a minimal subprocessor roster for Private deployments (note: most infra subcontractors only handle hardware and do not have logical access to tenant data). We'll provide a formal signed appendix — the draft I attached marks the entries that may touch telemetry/operational logs.

3) Egress/data flow: we can commit in the DPA addendum that customer inference payloads (inputs/outputs) are not exported to third regions or external analytics services. We propose the following clause (drafted in the attached PDF):
   "Redwood will not route, replicate, or export customer inference inputs or outputs to third‑party analytics services, nor will it transfer those data outside the contracted geo without Customer consent, except for temporary, encrypted snapshots required for forensic investigation with Customer approval."

4) Operator breakglass: for on‑prem, operator access is strictly limited to console guidance and remote runbooks; any elevated access requires a documented request from EdgeHealth SRE and a recorded, auditable session (mTLS + short‑lived credentials). We can include a 'breakglass playbook' annex with specific logging and notification SLAs.

Next steps I suggest:
- We send the redlined DPA annex (attached) plus the BYOK annex to your Legal.
- If they want, set a 30‑minute call with Ben and me to walk through the technical pieces (KMS handshake, network egress points).

Attached: redwood-byok-annex-draft.pdf; dpa-egress-redline.docx; edgehealth-network-sketch.png

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private deploy questions — BYOK, subprocessors, and egress

Priya / Ben — internal notes before we send to EdgeHealth Legal (forward in one message):

- BYOK wording: tighten the "no access" language to "Redwood personnel shall not possess, derive, or access customer plaintext nor hold unenveloped customer key material except as described in the Escrow Annex". This prevents ambiguous "no direct access" phrasing.
- Subprocessors: move storage/observability vendors into Appendix B and mark "no access to PII or inference payloads" except for metadata/metrics. Provide explicit retention windows for telemetry (30 days default, extendable by request).
- Egress clause: add an exception for "temporary, encrypted snapshots required for forensic investigation WITH CUSTOMER WRITTEN APPROVAL" and require that any such snapshot be redacted and deleted within X days (we should propose 14). EdgeHealth will likely push for zero‑snapshot; suggest 14 as compromise.
- Operational playbook: include a short checklist for breakglass: (1) Customer SRE ticket + attest, (2) RBAC elevation for specific host, (3) recorded session, (4) post‑mortem. This is our standard for private installs.

Ben — can you confirm the 14‑day snapshot deletion is technically feasible and whether we can add a retention flag so the customer can shorten it? Also confirm that operator sessions are recorded to our auditing pipeline and that those logs are tenant‑scoped.

Will draft a concise email to Legal that includes the three proposed bullets and attach the annexes; Priya, after you confirm language I'll send.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@edgehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeHealth Legal <legal@edgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK & egress contract clarification for EdgeHealth private deployment

Priya / Marissa — thanks for the thorough answers and the annex drafts. A couple of quick clarifications from Legal:

- Confirmed: EdgeHealth will accept the 14‑day encrypted snapshot window only if we retain the right to require deletion sooner on notice. Please add language that Customer may require immediate deletion in the event of an incident.
- Subprocessor appendix: please include a contact and SOC2 scope for each vendor listed that may touch telemetry.
- BYOK: Legal requested an explicit statement that Redwood will not hold any customer key material in any persistent form; a short sentence in the BYOK annex will satisfy them.

If you can incorporate those three items I'll route the updated annexes to Procurement for PO and Legal for signature. We should be able to move to DocuSign next week.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of InfoSec, EdgeHealth
